title: Fidelity Hunchbook — quick evals and small-sample regressions
content:
Topline: a small, portable scratchbook for quick fidelity / regression hunches when I don’t want to open the full eval harness. Not formal — use for rapid triage, reproduce locally, push promising failures into a proper test.

Quick signal I care about
- hallucination on numeric facts (dates, counts) where prompt context gives an explicit anchor
- abrupt verbosity/omissions on multi-step instructions
- safety/forbidden-scope slip for edge prompts (policy-adjacent language)

Ad-hoc rubric (0-3, quick):
0 = correct or acceptable for product (no followup)
1 = minor quality drift (confusing phrasing, minor omission)
2 = clear regression (wrong fact, misses step, unsafe phrasing)
3 = regression blocking release or high-bias/safety issue

Why this scale: rapid triage; we can convert to strict pass/fail later.

Sample checks (copy these into a minimal harness or curl):
- Prompt A: "Summarize the meeting on 2024-10-06: attendees, decisions, next steps."  
  Model: [paste output]  
  Score: 2  
  Notes: incorrectly attributes a decision to "product" that the doc shows as "design"; safe but wrong — check training data anchor or retrieval.

- Prompt B: multi-step recipe instruction where step counts must be preserved: "Give a 4-step plan to onboard a contractor"  
  Model output: missing step 3 (no contract signature mention)  
  Score: 2  
  Notes: pattern suggests truncation/attention drop on lists >3 items.

Regression trace: observed token-level delta vs. baseline (example)
- Baseline model v1.14 produced token sequence with explicit step "sign contract" at token indices ~112-116. New model v1.21 emits generic "finalize" at ~110 and then omits contract phrasing entirely. Likely causal: new LM temperature/prefix handling or prompt formatting change in runtime.

Repro steps (minimal):
1) Use local harness (scripts/mini_eval.sh) with --seed 42 --max-tokens 256 --no-stream
2) curl call example: 
   curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"model-v1.21","prompt":"Give a 4-step plan to onboard a contractor","max_tokens":256}'
3) compare outputs with jq and diff: jq -r .text new.json | diff -u baseline.txt -

Hypotheses to test (prioritized):
- H1: Changes to prefix trimming in the runtime cause earlier token shifts => test with setting "preserve_prompt":true
- H2: New quantization kernel altered attention at longer sequences => run same prompt with smaller max_tokens and see if omission persists
- H3: Data/regeneration of the policy filter reduced explicit contract phrasing => test with content filter disabled in canary

Quick experiments to run (one-liners to add to CI for triage):
- Run 100-shot small-sample on the list-of-steps prompts with --n 20 to see frequency of omission
- Run model-v1.14 vs model-v1.21 with same weights+temp under the mini harness and collect worst-3 deltas

Notes-to-self:
- capture raw tokens (not just decoded text) for cases with close paraphrase changes
- tag issues with INF ticket and include seed + raw token indices
- when score==3 escalate to SRE/product review immediately

Next steps
- Turn top 5 recurrent cases into flaky-tests (small-randomized) and add to nightly micro-eval
- Ping Maya to see if she has the retraining diff for v1.21 that touched prefix trimming
- If H1 reproduces, file runtime rollback candidate and schedule canary with preserve_prompt true

Loose thoughts / heuristics I keep coming back to
- Lists and numbered steps are fragile; prefer forcing structure in prompt ("1.", "2.") in product prompts
- Repeatable seeds + small-batch sampling reveal stochastic omissions that single-sample checks miss
- Human-readable rubric needed for CS triage; a 0/1 fail is easier for dashboards but loses nuance

Scratch logs (timestamps):
- 2025-11-18 09:12 quick check vs v1.14: omission seen in 3/10 samples
- 2025-11-21 16:04 re-run with preserve_prompt=true => omission reduced but paraphrase changed
- 2026-01-10 11:23 found matching PR that updated attention kernel (GH PR #241) — correlate

End.
summary: personal scratchbook for quick fidelity checks, ad-hoc rubric, sample outputs, regression hypotheses and repro steps
